annotations.tagline: Deprecated Spring Boot shopping-cart service with MongoDB-backed carts/items, REST endpoints, and optional Zipkin tracing
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
Deprecated microservice in the `microservices-demo`/Weaveworks shop that manages customer carts and line items in MongoDB. It is a long-running Java 8 Spring Boot app packaged as a JAR and container image ([README.md](carts/README.md), [pom.xml](carts/pom.xml), [Dockerfile](carts/Dockerfile)).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- Handwritten REST controllers expose `/health`, `/carts/{customerId}`, `/carts/{customerId}/merge`, and `/carts/{customerId}/items...` ([HealthCheckController](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/HealthCheckController.java), [CartsController](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/CartsController.java), [ItemsController](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/ItemsController.java)).
- `ItemRepository` is exported via Spring Data REST, so `/items` is also part of the public surface; `CartRepository` is explicitly hidden (`exported = false`) ([ItemRepository](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/repositories/ItemRepository.java), [CartRepository](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/repositories/CartRepository.java), [api-spec/routes.json](carts/api-spec/routes.json)).

## Domain entities owned
- `Cart` stores a `customerId` and a DB-ref list of `Item` documents ([Cart.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/entities/Cart.java)).
- `Item` stores `itemId`, `quantity`, and `unitPrice` ([Item.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/entities/Item.java)).
- `HealthCheck` is the response model for `/health` ([HealthCheck.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/entities/HealthCheck.java)).

## Important business rules
- A missing cart is created on first access; cart lookup falls back to a new `Cart` when no result exists ([CartResource.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/cart/CartResource.java), [FirstResultOrDefault.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/action/FirstResultOrDefault.java)).
- Adding an item creates a new stored item when absent, otherwise increments quantity and merges the update ([ItemsController.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/ItemsController.java), [FoundItem.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/item/FoundItem.java)).
- `merge` copies items from a session cart into the customer cart and then deletes the session cart ([CartsController.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/CartsController.java)).
- `/health` reports app and database status; database failures flip the database check to `err` ([HealthCheckController.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/controllers/HealthCheckController.java)).

## Persistence
- MongoDB is configured through `spring.data.mongodb.uri=mongodb://${db:carts-db}:27017/data` ([application.properties](carts/src/main/resources/application.properties)).
- The code and Dredd seed data use `cart` and `item` collections/documents ([Cart.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/entities/Cart.java), [Item.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/entities/Item.java), [api-spec/hooks.js](carts/api-spec/hooks.js)).

## External dependencies
- Optional Zipkin tracing is configured with `spring.zipkin.baseUrl` and `spring.zipkin.enabled` ([application.properties](carts/src/main/resources/application.properties), [docker-compose-zipkin.yml](carts/docker-compose-zipkin.yml)).
- Prometheus request latency metrics are exposed via `HTTPMonitoringInterceptor` and `@EnablePrometheusEndpoint` ([HTTPMonitoringInterceptor.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/middleware/HTTPMonitoringInterceptor.java), [CartApplication.java](carts/src/main/java/works/weave/socks/cart/CartApplication.java)).

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Go HTTP catalogue service for Socks Shop that filters sock products by tag, serves images, and reads MySQL.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
Deprecated Go service for the Socks Shop demo that serves sock catalogue data over HTTP. The main binary starts in `cmd/cataloguesvc/main.go`, wires the service in `service.go`, and mounts the HTTP routes in `transport.go`.

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
REST endpoints: GET `/catalogue`, `/catalogue/size`, `/catalogue/{id}`, `/tags`, `/health`, `/metrics`, plus static files under `/catalogue/images/` (`transport.go`). The request contract supports `tags`, `sort`, `page`, and `size` query parameters (`transport.go`, `endpoints.go`). The documented API also matches `api-spec/catalogue.json`.

## Domain entities owned
`Sock` is the main product record. `Tag` values are the catalogue filters stored in the MySQL `tag` table. `Health` is the health payload returned by `/health` for the app and DB (`service.go`).

## Important business rules
List and Count filter by comma-separated tag names using OR conditions in SQL (`service.go`). `sort` defaults to `id`; any non-empty value is lowercased and passed into the ORDER BY clause (`transport.go`, `service.go`). Pagination is 1-indexed: `pageNum` or `pageSize` of 0 returns an empty slice (`service.go`). `Get` returns `ErrNotFound` when an ID is missing and the HTTP encoder turns that into a 404 (`service.go`, `transport.go`). `/health` reports `catalogue` and `catalogue-db` statuses, with DB failure shown as `err` (`service.go`). Zipkin tracing is optional and only enabled when `ZIPKIN` is set (`cmd/cataloguesvc/main.go`).

## Persistence
The default DSN is `catalogue_user:default_password@tcp(catalogue-db:3306)/socksdb` (`cmd/cataloguesvc/main.go`). The bundled seed script creates `sock`, `tag`, and `sock_tag`, loads the initial rows, and grants access to `catalogue_user` (`docker/catalogue-db/data/dump.sql`). The application only performs read queries and health pings; writes happen during database container initialization.

## External dependencies
MySQL for persistence, Zipkin for distributed tracing, Prometheus for `/metrics`, and Go kit / Gorilla mux for the runtime stack (`cmd/cataloguesvc/main.go`, `transport.go`).

annotations.tagline: Node.js/Express storefront for microservices-demo that serves static pages and proxies cart, catalogue, orders, and user APIs.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`front-end` is the browser-facing storefront for microservices-demo. It serves static HTML/JS from `public/` and hosts an Express app that proxies browser actions to backend services (`server.js`, `public/js/client.js`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- Cart: `GET/POST/DELETE /cart`, `DELETE /cart/:id`, `POST /cart/update` (`api/cart/index.js`)
- Catalogue: `GET /catalogue*`, `GET /catalogue/images*`, `GET /tags` (`api/catalogue/index.js`)
- Orders: `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/*`, `POST /orders` (`api/orders/index.js`)
- User/auth: `GET /login`, `POST /register`, customer/address/card routes (`api/user/index.js`)
- Metrics: `GET /metrics` (`api/metrics/index.js`)
- No queues or GraphQL endpoints.

## Domain entities owned
- No durable product/order/customer datastore in this repo.
- Session-scoped customer identity lives in `req.session.customerId`.
- The `logged_in` cookie signals authenticated state and drives UI behavior.

## Important business rules
- Missing `logged_in` clears `customerId`; cart and order actions reject unauthenticated users.
- In `development`, `?custId=` can override the session customer for testing (`helpers/index.js`).
- Login and registration both set `customerId`, write the `logged_in` cookie, and merge the anonymous cart via `/merge?sessionId=...`.
- Checkout depends on saved address and card data; the basket page disables ordering when either is missing (`public/basket.html`).

## Persistence
- Default sessions use the local `express-session` store.
- If `SESSION_REDIS` is set, sessions use `connect-redis` with host `session-db` (`config.js`).

## External dependencies
- `catalogue` for item lookup, product images, and tags.
- `carts` for cart contents, item mutations, and cart merge.
- `orders` for order history and order creation.
- `user` for login, registration, customer, address, and card data.

annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
Deprecated Locust-based load and integration test harness for the microservices-demo application. It simulates browser-like user journeys against a host passed on the command line and runs to completion after a configured number of requests ([README.md](load-test/README.md), [locustfile.py](load-test/locustfile.py)).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
No inbound HTTP API, queue, or GraphQL surface is exposed by this repo. The public interface is the `runLocust.sh` CLI/entrypoint with `-h`, `-c`, `-r`, and `-d` options, which the Docker image uses as its `ENTRYPOINT` ([runLocust.sh](load-test/runLocust.sh), [Dockerfile](load-test/Dockerfile)).

## Domain entities owned
None. The test is stateless. It reads a catalogue payload, picks a random item id, and then exercises the target application's browse, login, cart, basket, and order flows ([locustfile.py](load-test/locustfile.py)).

## Important business rules
- `TARGET_HOST` is required; the wrapper exits if it is missing and also verifies the host returns HTTP 200 before launching Locust.
- `LOCUST_FILE` can be overridden via environment variable; otherwise `locustfile.py` is used.
- The scripted journey always hits `/catalogue`, `/`, `/login`, `/category.html`, `/detail.html?id=...`, `/cart`, `/basket.html`, and `/orders`.
- `push.sh` publishes Docker images only for master snapshot builds and tagged releases, using `master-${COMMIT:0:8}` and `latest` tags ([push.sh](load-test/push.sh)).

## Persistence
None. There is no database, cache, or message broker in this repository.

## External dependencies
Runtime depends on Locust (`locustio`) and the Python 2.7 base image; the container also installs `pyzmq` and `faker` ([Dockerfile](load-test/Dockerfile)). The test depends on whatever application is exposed at `TARGET_HOST`.

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Spring Boot orders service that creates orders, charges payment, triggers shipping, and stores order records in MongoDB.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`orders` is the deprecated order-management service in `microservices-demo`. It accepts order-creation requests, resolves linked customer/address/card/item resources, charges payment, triggers shipping, and persists the completed order in MongoDB (`README.md`, `src/main/java/works/weave/socks/orders/controllers/OrdersController.java`, `src/main/resources/application.properties`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- `POST /orders` in `OrdersController` creates a new order from `NewOrderResource`.
- Spring Data REST exposes the `CustomerOrderRepository` collection/item endpoints under `/orders` and the customer lookup under `/orders/search/customerId`.
- `GET /health` returns application and database health information.
- Prometheus metrics are served from the configured metrics servlet path, default `/metrics`.
- No GraphQL or message queues are defined in this repo.

## Domain entities owned
- `CustomerOrder` is the persisted order aggregate.
- `Cart` and `Item` are Mongo documents; `Customer`, `Address`, `Card`, and `Shipment` are order-related payload objects used during request handling.
- `PaymentRequest` and `PaymentResponse` define the contract to the payment service.

## Important business rules
- `POST /orders` rejects requests missing `customer`, `address`, `card`, or `items` by throwing `InvalidOrderException`.
- The service fetches address, customer, card, and items asynchronously, then computes `total` as line-item sum plus fixed shipping `4.99`.
- Payment must succeed before shipping is created; a null or unauthorised `PaymentResponse` raises `PaymentDeclinedException`.
- Shipping uses the parsed customer id from the linked customer resource href.
- The `HealthCheck` endpoint marks the database status `err` if the Mongo `buildInfo` command fails.

## Persistence
- Orders are stored in MongoDB via `spring.data.mongodb.uri=mongodb://${db:orders-db}:27017/data`.
- `CustomerOrderRepository` persists `CustomerOrder` documents and exposes a `findByCustomerId` search.
- `HealthCheckController` uses `MongoTemplate` to probe the same database.

## External dependencies
- The service calls the payment service at `http://payment.../paymentAuth` and the shipping service at `http://shipping.../shipping` (the domain suffix is optional and driven by config).
- Tracing is exported to Zipkin when enabled via Spring Cloud Sleuth/Zipkin.
- Outbound HTTP can be routed through an HTTP proxy when `proxy.host` and `proxy.port` are set.

metadata.description: Stateless Go HTTP service under `cmd/paymentsvc`; exposes JSON REST endpoints plus `/metrics` and optional Zipkin tracing.

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Go payment-authorization service with `/paymentAuth`, health/metrics endpoints, threshold declines, and optional Zipkin tracing.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`payment` is the microservices-demo payment authorization service. It accepts JSON payment requests and returns approved or declined results based on an amount threshold (`cmd/paymentsvc/main.go`, `service.go`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
REST over HTTP:
- `POST /paymentAuth` authorizes a payment.
- `GET /health` returns a health payload.
- `GET /metrics` exposes Prometheus metrics.
The canonical Swagger contract is in `api-spec/payment.json`. The code also returns a `message` field on `Authorisation` in addition to `authorised` (`transport.go`, `endpoints.go`, `service.go`).

## Domain entities owned
`AuthoriseRequest` carries `amount`; `Authorisation` carries `authorised` and `message`; `Health` carries `service`, `status`, and `time`.

## Important business rules
`service.go` rejects `amount == 0` and `amount < 0` with `ErrInvalidPaymentAmount`. Amounts `<= declineOverAmount` are authorised; larger amounts are declined with a formatted message. The default threshold is `105` from `-decline` in `cmd/paymentsvc/main.go`. Tracing is disabled when `ZIPKIN` is empty and enabled with a Zipkin HTTP collector when it is set.

## Persistence
None. The service is stateless and keeps no DB, queue, or topic state.

## External dependencies
Optional Zipkin tracing uses `ZIPKIN` and `zipkin.NewHTTPCollector`; the local compose file points at `http://zipkin:9411/api/v1/spans` (`docker-compose-zipkin.yml`). The container runs the HTTP server on port `8080` and the compose file maps it to host port `8082`.

domain_attributes.meaning: Zero and negative amounts are rejected; positive amounts at or below `declineOverAmount` are authorised, otherwise the payment is declined.

domain_attributes.meaning: CLI flag `-decline` sets the default amount ceiling; higher amounts are declined.

metadata.name: queue-master
metadata.description: Spring Boot service with RabbitMQ consumer wiring, custom health reporting, and Prometheus metrics. The Docker worker-spawning path exists but its calls are commented out.

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Spring Boot shipping-queue consumer that exposes health and Prometheus endpoints.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`queue-master` is a deprecated `microservices-demo` service that consumes shipping work from RabbitMQ and reports health/metrics for the stack. The repo is a Spring Boot 1.4 / Java 8 application packaged as a JAR (`pom.xml`, `QueueMasterApplication.java`). The README says it reads from the shipping queue and historically spawned worker containers, though the container-spawning calls are commented out in `ShippingTaskHandler.java`.

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- `GET /health` in `HealthCheckController.java` returns a map containing `queue-master` and `queue-master-rabbitmq` health entries.
- `GET /prometheus` is exposed through the custom Actuator endpoint in `PrometheusEndpoint.java` / `PrometheusMvcEndpoint.java`.
- RabbitMQ consumer wiring is in `ShippingConsumerConfiguration.java`; the service listens on the `shipping-task` queue.

## Domain entities owned
- `Shipment` (`src/main/java/works/weave/socks/shipping/entities/Shipment.java`) is the AMQP payload type. It carries `id` and `name`.
- `HealthCheck` (`src/main/java/works/weave/socks/queuemaster/entities/HealthCheck.java`) is the JSON DTO returned by `/health` with `service`, `status`, and `date`.

## Important business rules
- The consumer is bound to the hard-coded `shipping-task` queue name in both the RabbitMQ configuration and listener container.
- `/health` always reports the app as `OK`; RabbitMQ is also reported as `OK` unless the connection probe throws an `AmqpException`, in which case it is set to `err`.
- The active runtime uses `RabbitTemplate.execute(...)` only as a connection probe; there is no publish path in the current code.
- Prometheus metrics are backed by a custom `CollectorRegistry` and `PrometheusMetricWriter`.

## Persistence
- No database, document store, or cache was found. The service is stateless aside from RabbitMQ connectivity and in-memory Prometheus registry state.

## External dependencies
- RabbitMQ is the broker the service connects to (`spring.rabbitmq.host=rabbitmq` in `src/main/resources/application.properties`).
- Spring Boot Actuator and Prometheus client libraries provide the `/prometheus` metrics endpoint.
- The codebase contains dormant Docker container-spawning logic in `DockerSpawner.java`, but it is currently not invoked from the active message handler.

domain_attributes.meaning: The health endpoint reports the app as `OK` and flips the RabbitMQ entry to `err` if the AMQP connection probe throws.
The built-in Actuator health endpoint is disabled so the custom `/health` controller is used instead.

Both the RabbitTemplate and listener container are wired to the same hard-coded shipping queue name.

metadata.name: shipping
metadata.description: Stateless Spring Boot HTTP service that accepts shipping requests, publishes shipment jobs to RabbitMQ, and exposes custom health and metrics endpoints.

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Spring Boot shipping service that publishes shipment jobs to RabbitMQ and exposes health/metrics endpoints.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`shipping` is the deprecated shipping service for the `microservices-demo` / Socks Shop demo. It boots as a Spring Boot application and serves shipping-related HTTP endpoints (`README.md`, `pom.xml`, `src/main/java/works/weave/socks/shipping/ShippingServiceApplication.java`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- `GET /shipping`, `GET /shipping/{id}`, `POST /shipping`, and `GET /health` are defined in `ShippingController`.
- `GET /metrics` is exposed by a Prometheus servlet registered in `PrometheusAutoConfiguration`.
- `POST /shipping` accepts a `Shipment` payload and attempts to enqueue it for downstream processing.

## Domain entities owned
- `Shipment` has `id` and `name` fields and is the payload accepted by `POST /shipping`.
- `HealthCheck` models each entry in the custom `/health` response with `service`, `status`, and `date`.

## Important business rules
- `POST /shipping` publishes to RabbitMQ queue `shipping-task`; if publish fails, the request still succeeds and the shipment is returned (`ShippingController`).
- `/health` always returns two checks: `shipping-rabbitmq` and `shipping`; RabbitMQ status becomes `err` if the broker call throws `AmqpException`.
- Request latency metrics are recorded with Prometheus, but `/error` requests are excluded and labels use `spring.application.name`.
- Zipkin tracing is disabled by default in `application.properties` and enabled in the Zipkin docker-compose example.

## Persistence
No local database, repository, or ORM layer is present. The service is stateless and hands off shipment work through RabbitMQ.

## External dependencies
RabbitMQ is configured through `spring.rabbitmq.host=rabbitmq` and used for the `shipping-task` queue/exchange pair. Zipkin is configured through `spring.zipkin.baseUrl=http://${zipkin_host:zipkin}:9411/` and `spring.zipkin.enabled`. Prometheus is used for the `/metrics` endpoint (`src/main/resources/application.properties`, `src/main/java/works/weave/socks/shipping/configuration/PrometheusAutoConfiguration.java`).

domain_attributes.meaning: The `/health` endpoint reports RabbitMQ as `OK` when the AMQP connection callback succeeds, and changes it to `err` when an `AmqpException` is caught.
Zipkin tracing is disabled by default in `application.properties` and enabled in the docker-compose example by setting `ZIPKIN_ENABLED=true`.
The service name label for Prometheus request latency metrics comes from `spring.application.name`; the interceptor defaults to `orders` but the application sets it to `shipping`.
Prometheus request latency is not recorded for `/error`; other matched routes are measured.

glossary.definition: The broader demo product this repo belongs to; the Docker label calls this service `Socks Shop: Shipping`.

annotations.tagline: Deprecated Go HTTP service for user accounts, with MongoDB-backed customers, cards, addresses, and HAL links.
annotations.capability_sheet:
## Purpose
`microservices-demo/user` is the deprecated Go user-account service for the microservices-demo stack. It stores customer profiles plus related cards and addresses, and serves them over HTTP/HAL (`README.md`, `main.go`, `api/transport.go`).

## Public surface (REST/GraphQL/queues)
- GET `/login` uses HTTP Basic auth.
- POST `/register` creates a new customer.
- GET `/health` reports app and database status.
- GET/POST `/customers`, GET `/customers/{id}`.
- GET `/customers/{id}/addresses`, GET `/customers/{id}/cards`.
- POST `/addresses`, POST `/cards`.
- DELETE `/customers/{id}` removes the customer and associated records.
- `/metrics` is exposed for Prometheus scraping.
Responses are HAL JSON.

## Domain entities owned
- `users.User` with embedded `users.Address` and `users.Card`.
- HAL `Links` for `customer`, `address`, and `card`.
- Mongo wrappers for persisted customer/address/card documents.

## Important business rules
- Login hashes `password` with the stored `salt` and returns `Unauthorized` on mismatch.
- Register/PostUser always create a fresh salt before hashing.
- Card numbers are masked before returning or logging.
- A `userID` on address/card creation links that record to a customer; an empty `userID` leaves it unattached.
- Deleting a customer cascades to its addresses and cards; deleting an address/card removes its reference from customers first.

## Persistence
- MongoDB database `users` with `customers`, `addresses`, and `cards` collections.
- The backend is selected with `-database=mongodb` / `USER_DATABASE`.
- `docker/user-db/` builds a seeded MongoDB image for demo/local runs.

## External dependencies
- Optional Zipkin tracing via `ZIPKIN` and `docker-compose-zipkin.yml`.
- HAL links are built from `HATEAOS` / `link-domain`.

domain_attributes.meaning: The customer GET endpoints return embedded `addresses` or `cards` when the path suffix asks for that related collection; otherwise they return the user object or an empty shell.
A blank ID means list all customers/cards/addresses; a non-empty ID means fetch a single record.
Deleting `customers` cascades to the customer's addresses and cards; deleting `addresses` or `cards` first removes that ObjectID from customer documents and then deletes the target document.
A blank `userID` creates an unattached address/card; a non-empty `userID` appends the new ObjectID to the customer's `addresses` or `cards` array.
Startup fails if no backend is selected; `mongodb` is the only registered database backend in this repo.
